qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Irish banking duopoly with Bank of Ireland following foreign bank exits (KBC, Ulster Bank). Sticky, low-cost domestic deposit base provides switching cost advantage in daily retail and commercial banking; however, pricing on retail mortgages faces ongoing domestic political and regulatory scrutiny.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). AIB Group benefits from an Irish retail banking duopoly and sticky domestic deposits, but commercial banking possesses a structurally short competitive advantage period (Tier 4 fade rate). As ECB policy rates normalize downward, net interest margins face cyclical contraction, while digital neo-banks (e.g., Revolut) continue to disintermediate high-margin payment and transactional workflows.
qualitative.evidence: AIB Group commands ~30-32% share of Irish mortgages and >35% of domestic deposits after Ulster Bank and KBC exited the market. While ROTE peaked at >20% in 2024-2025 during the peak of ECB rate hikes, 10-year average ROE is modest at ~7.5-8.0%, weighed down by zero-rate era compression and 2020 pandemic provisions. Net interest income accounts for the vast majority of operating income, leaving earnings exposed to the ECB monetary easing cycle.
